title: Мария (Mariya)
content: I didn’t have to die for God to speak to me. I experienced a three-day JUDGMENT while fully alive and conscious. My name is Maria. Right now, as I write this, I’m 25, but it all started four years ago. I was in deep depression because of my past. I won’t go into details, but here is a few words for context. I was born into a poor family where all relationships were built on harshness and hatred. My mother beat me for any reason and psychologically terrorized me every day throughout my childhood. It was real psychological abuse. Sometimes I went to school with bruises and welts, hiding them under my clothes. My brothers drank alcohol constantly, along with my father, who practically lived on the stairwell of our apartment building. They were basically homeless together. Our home was always filled with shouting, fights, and physical and emotional pain. The neighbors and school knew about our family’s situation, but no one really did anything about it. Because of this, I was bullied by other kids and even sometimes by teachers. During my university years, I was stalked for several years by two strangers who each separately physically assaulted me. Then came my first intense love and the breakup. Around the same time, within a year of each other, both my brothers died. At some point, I couldn’t cope with that cruel reality anymore. I began smoking weed occasionally, dropped out of university in the middle of my fourth year (even though I was a straight-A student and the group leader), and was crushed by the image of the smiley, perfect girl who had it all together. I was good at hiding everything behind a smile, but inside, I was dying. I wanted to leave everything behind and escape my home country, and that’s what I did. I flew away with a young man who showed me more kindness than anyone I’d ever known. I fell in love with him. At first, I felt euphoria. But when I was left alone with myself, I had nowhere left to run from what was happening inside me. The pain stopped being purely psychological. Physical symptoms appeared, constantly mimicking a heart attack with unbearable, aching chest pain. Then it started happening. I thought a lot about death. I couldn’t see the meaning in life anymore. The only thing keeping me here was my love for my boyfriend, who later became my husband. The pain was unbearable, but I endured it for him. Then I drew a picture inspired by a song, symbolizing my inner pain and suffering. I added one detail of my own. It was a child looking through a small crack into the darkness. In that darkness, I drew a glowing lightbulb and labeled it simply: "God". That one random detail changed my entire life. Up until then, I had been an atheist for years. That drawing was just a desperate cry for help, a final hope for saving my soul. I read every book on psychology and psychiatry I could find to help myself. Nothing worked. At one point, I thought about killing myself in the bathroom, but something stopped me. Later, I went outside, and something in my mind *clicked*. I began perceiving everything around me as a mirror of my inner world. As I walked, everything I saw all formed a message for me. This included numbers, signs, words on ads, clothes of passersby, cars with writing on them, fragments of conversations, shapes, objects, nature, animals, random occurrences. Everything became trigger elements that aligned and spoke to me. And this was despite the fact that I was in a foreign country with a language I didn’t understand. The environment was communicating with me. It was showing me my inner world, and I didn’t like what I saw. I walked down the street in broad daylight, and wherever I passed, streetlights flickered on as if guiding me, just like in my drawing. It scared me, but I knew my life had to change. But it was only the beginning. These spontaneous insights and synchronicities began manifesting differently. I could struggle with a question for a long time, read countless books. When I least expected it, it seemed as if it would speak to me again through images, symbols, and text. Sometimes entire paragraphs or pages would speak directly to me. It wasn’t like reading a book normally. I’d slip into a kind of trance. It was as if the book already knew what I would think. This started happening with music, movies, TV shows, even scientific articles. It it wasn’t random. Everything was talking to me. At times, my awareness would shift, and I’d receive a message. Occasionally, it would fade, and I’d convince myself it was all in my head. But, the harder I tried to forget, the louder the truth became. Sometimes I gave up and tried to return to my old ways: weed, alcohol, suffering over the past, depression. I tried everything to stop seeing and hearing, because killing my ego and letting go of the illusions I’d lived with my entire life was painful. And I still suffered and the pain only grew. Back then, I had a blog where I wrote a few posts days before returning home. The first post was simple: just a vomiting emoji. It symbolized how tired I was of dwelling on the past. I was physically sick of a certain person from my past. Many of my insights at the time revolved around them because, back then, my unrequited love and failed relationship were my deepest, bleeding wounds. I was shown the truth behind our relationship. I realized everything I’d believed was just a mask. I expressed my feelings through that simple emoji because I didn’t want to accept the truth because it hurt too much. I was exhausted, beyond words. The second post was different. I made a drawing into a digital collage. It showed a cloudy sky, a crying eye, a white dove with an olive branch, and two people embracing. I captioned it: "Weather sensitivity is when the sky screams and cries with you." I didn’t know my posts could materialize like the drawing with the lightbulb had. The day before my flight back home, I started reading a book about psychotherapy under altered states of consciousness. It felt like normal reading at first, but certain phrases, acted as triggers and stuck with me. I don’t remember them exactly, but the general idea was: "No matter what happens, stay calm and pretend everything is fine." Another trigger was having something to say, and I would have to speak. There was also an exercise about overcoming the fear of a plane crash. The idea being, that I am not the pilot, I can’t control the plane, so panicking is pointless. Later, I understood why. My husband and I arrived at the airport. It was an ordinary day. I had quit drinking, smoking, drugs, and hallucinogens. It was just a normal day. My husband rested his head in my lap, and I massaged his temples. Then, for no reason, tears started streaming down my cheeks. I didn’t stop them, thinking it might help reduce my cortisol levels. For 15 minutes straight, I cried non-stop with no obvious trigger. I should have calmed down quickly, but the tears wouldn’t stop. Then I noticed the weather was cloudy and drizzling. It was exactly like my post about weather sensitivity. Two hours passed, and I still hadn’t stopped crying. I’d manage a short break before the tears resumed. We boarded the plane, and for the entire two-hour flight, I sobbed. Then, at our connecting airport, something unexplainable happened. I was still crying. A thought crystallized, "It’s time to let myself cry out everything I’ve buried my whole life." I had always suppressed my pain, forced myself to be strong, run from my emotions. Now, I had to feel it all. And I did. At the airport entrance, the security gate (the kind that scans for weapons) was beeping erratically, flashing and malfunctioning. All the computers in the airport were glitching; some frozen, some flickering. The machines were going haywire, pulsing like emergency lights. We were let through without a proper check. We tried storing luggage, but the locker kept opening and closing. This went on for 20 minutes. Then I remembered the book’s advice, "Stay calm, no matter what. Trust the process." And as I walked through the airport, my surroundings spoke to me. My consciousness seemed to split—one part of me stayed with my husband, moving forward, while another part perceived everything beyond. It was like seeing not just the surface of reality, but its truth. It was a judgement review of my life. I was on trial, but not in an earthly sense. My life was on display, and I was judging myself through objects, words, ads, and random events. Everything was washed together in synchronicities. I saw my mistakes such as how I held onto old pain, hatred, resentment, guilt, and regret. Even in unrelated conversations between strangers, I received messages, as if their words were for me. I saw where I had hurt others, and where I had been hurt but never healed. I was shown my biggest mistakes; moments I could have acted out of love instead of ego. The whole time, I kept crying. I couldn’t deny the truth—I didn’t even try. I accepted it, even through tears. And with each revelation, my body revolted. After the first wave, when my stomach was empty, I dry-heaved bile. It wasn’t food poisoning. I remembered the vomiting emoji post as purification. My body was expelling a lifetime of unprocessed pain, trauma, resentment. Every cell hurt. The deeper the insight, the more violent the purging. That was just Day One of my judgment. All together there were three days. Our next flight was overnight. Surprisingly, the plane was nearly empty, maybe 20 passengers plus the crew. I was still crying, still nauseous, and still aching. I felt a new sensation as my body was compressing from the plane’s speed. For the first hour, I kept running to the bathroom as insights hit me; each followed by retching. Hunched in my seat, clutching my knees, I wished for it all to end. But, it was far from over. Then, I felt an urge to look out the window and froze. We were flying over cities at night; their streets lined with lights. Before my eyes, some lights turned off, while others turned on. They were forming pictures. The patterns shifted in real time, reacting to my thoughts by answering my unspoken questions. It was a continuation of my life review with my thoughts and my false beliefs displayed as moving light. I turned to show my husband, but the entire plane was asleep. Even the crew wasn’t looking. I was alone, watching the lights draw my destiny. Then I saw a man who looked like one of my late brothers. The feeling of grief hit hard. The lights showed me moments I’d been indifferent when I could’ve acted with love. Shame within burned me because now, I couldn’t make it right since he was gone. Suddenly, the plane accelerated violently into turbulence. Still, everyone slept. The light-pattern showed my lifeline as becoming jagged and breaking. The plane tilted downward. I genuinely thought we were crashing. "Fine," I thought, "if I die, I die." But an invisible force turned my head to my husband, to the man resembling my brother, and to every person around me. A realization struck me that I was responsible for them, too. Our consciousnesses were connected, influencing each other. Silence hung heavy, as if the world was holding its breath just for me. A phrase from the book echoed, "If your family doesn’t raise you, the tribe will." Strangers were my teachers. We’re all linked. The plane kept speeding along. I remembered another line, "You’re not the pilot. You can’t control the crash." But what if we were crashing? My suicidal thoughts had never considered how my death would hurt others. Then, my lifeline snapped. A skull-and-crossbones flashed in the lights. Genuine terror gripped me. "Alive, I could change. Dead, I couldn’t." For minutes, I endured sheer horror until I begged that "I want to LIVE." I sobbed, praying to God to stop this. Instantly everything was calm and the stars reappeared. The lights formed a circled cross which I felt was God’s reassurance. The cross symbolized Christ’s sacrifice; the circle, His eternity. The plane’s ordeal had taught me, to trust Him like a passenger trusts the pilot. Day Three: We wandered a massive, crowded airport with nowhere to rest. For the first time, I confessing my regrets to my husband. With every "I forgive you," a weight lifted. In a capsule hotel, sleep was impossible. In every sound, smell, or conversation my judgment continued. I saw how I neglected myself by skipping meals, drowning in coffee, and choosing distractions over peace. Even in sleep, the trial persisted. Exhausted, we went to a mall. I saw a huge signs that read "FINISH LINE". Then I saw my university years, my ex-"everything" resurfaced. In a café, fate mirrored my fantasy. I had a final talk with the man who’d broken me. Lights, words, even the décor replayed our toxic dynamic reminding me of his gaslighting and my reaction of people-pleasing. But I couldn’t leave. My body locked up, magnetized to the table. The pain, nausea, and tears multiplied a thousand-fold. A voice whispered, "He’s not here." I tried to throw myself down the stairs, but couldn’t move. The book’s warning returned, "Even if you want to die, you won’t be able to." Time slowed. My thoughts pared down to one choice, I could choose to stay trapped or to move forward. When ten strangers, who resembled my old friends filed in, I had to decide. My husband’s outstretched hand was my lifeline. I took it. Strength returned. The pain eased. I ate without vomiting, for the first time in days. On the 12-hour bus ride home, I heard a whisper, "Jesus is near." Only I heard it. Repeat lullabies of peace. In the post-judgment phase, God kept speaking softly now. Once, high, I saw my aura was damaged. Another time, my head turned toward an icon that represented shame for my weakness. Then, His love broke through. I saw a heart-shaped cloud in the sky. There were no conditions, nothing to earn, and no pretending. I just love. Later, a door labeled "Staff Only" lit up. I felt this was God’s call for me to serve. My drawings manifested, too. Months later, I drew a cross on a woman’s spine. I knew that she had chronic back pain exactly where cross was positioned. I realized that my window’s light formed that same cross. I felt streetlights now follow me as they were guiding and affirming to me. I talk to God daily. Some things can’t be explained. Only lived. This was my judgment before death. And it was also my rebirth. There were other transcendent experiences, including the story with the icons. Ultimately, this led me to completely give up alcohol, smoking, and everything that harms my body and mind; including toxic relationships with people, certain friends, and relatives. This helped to improve my sleep. Every time I followed God’s will, even when it didn’t seem logical, I received confirmation from Him that I was doing the right thing and that everything was truly good. The opposite also held true; when I acted against His will and ignored the signs, it led to unpleasant consequences. I began praying often for myself, for loved ones, and even for strangers. Sometimes, when I focused deeply in prayer, every cell in my body would vibrate, and I’d feel a pleasant trembling throughout my being. This state also arose when I helped others, heard important messages, or listened to testimonies about God or near-death experiences. It felt like sacred confirmation of their words. When I read the Bible or anything related to God, that same indescribable trembling would fill me. Sometimes it happened when I felt sad or disappointed in people. God comforted and supported me, not just in this way but in many others. Sometimes, when I prayed, God answered immediately; other times, later. Prayer has a powerful effect on the environment and people. There were many instances where what I prayed for happened very quickly. Once, my husband fell seriously ill. Tests showed nothing wrong, yet he worsened by the hour. That night, as he slept, I prayed fervently, imagining angels helping and a white light healing him. At that moment, he turned to me in his sleep, smiled, and took my hand. It was as if his soul responded instantly. The next morning, we went to another clinic where tests finally revealed the issue, leading to his recovery. Another time, my husband needed my help with work but wanted to hide it from his employer, as the job involved serious financial decisions. I refused to lie, though the chances of the employer agreeing seemed zero. I prayed for a solution without deceit. The very next day, the employer called and offered to train me so we could take shifts, sparing my husband from working 24-25 hours straight. I was stunned. Such offers had never happened before. I knew it was God’s doing. For this and so much more, I am endlessly grateful. Life changed profoundly. Miracles became something I woke and slept with. I began seeing cause and effect in events such that even a random phrase could alter everything. Now, when something happens, I no longer ask, "Why me?" I know why. I glimpsed a fragment of divine balance and harmony. What seems like chaos to us is God’s perfect order. Wherever I am, whatever I feel or do is the exact experience my soul needs; measured to the millimeter. New states emerged. Sometimes I’d wake up praying or reciting scripture in my sleep. My dreams grew vivid and spiritually charged. There is enough there to fill a book. Once, I was prescribed a strong sedative for back pain. Due to my existing bradycardia, my pulse dropped dangerously low in sleep. I felt my heart slowing, nearing arrest. In the dream, I saw the room not with my eyes but with my soul. Sleep paralysis held me; I couldn’t move or call my awake husband for help. Panicked, I cried, "Lord, help me!" Instantly, I regained control and woke, confirming my irregular heartbeat. Another time, my heart stopped in sleep. I saw the room and my sleeping husband. I told him, "My heart is stopping. I’m dying." His soul replied, "Go to Him!" I turned and saw a slightly open door, warm light streaming through. As I reached to open it, I returned to my body and woke. I don’t know if I was near death, but my pulse often drops below 40, confirmed by Holter tests. It is a lifelong reality for me. I’ve tried to summarize briefly, but these experiences were far deeper and more numerous. The essence? It has taught me to change my life for the better; love and cherish it, and help others because we’re all in the same boat. Perhaps my story of pain, guilt, and God’s miraculous influence will inspire others. I know what it’s like to be misunderstood or labeled as crazy. I continue holding a truth that can’t be unseen. Remember, you’re not alone. If this helps even one person, I’ll be happier. Thank you for letting me be heard and perhaps understood. May God bless everyone touched by this message.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Uncertain, Suicide attempt, Illness, trauma or other condition not considered life threatening
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, There was a feeling of inner knowing. Packets of knowledge seemed to unpack in my consciousness. My senses were heightened many times over. While everything that happened to me might seem like madness, when it was happening, I didn't even think it was supernatural. It felt normal, as if my soul knew things my human logic couldn't grasp.
elements.At what time during the experience were: I was 100% conscious the whole time. For three days of the experience, I was literally connected to the consciousness of God. This was the largest and longest of all my transcendent experiences.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Time seemed to go faster or slower than usual, At different moments, time either flowed normally or accelerated or slowed down unimaginably, depending on the context of the situation and the specific insight.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I began to see the world around me more vividly, noticing things I had previously overlooked. The world became richer in colors, sounds, sensations, and even taste.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: While others in the bus or reality couldn't hear it, I constantly heard the repeating words "Jesus is nearby" with background meditative noise.
elements.Did you seem to be aware of things going: Yes, and the facts have been checked out
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, I had experiences regarding my brother who died in a plane crash. I felt the presence of living acquaintances from university in that cafe. But physically, they were unfamiliar people who weren't there by accident.
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, The first time I saw an unusually bright, warm light was in real life when this first started happening with me. It was as if I saw photons, and an unusually brighter warm glow from the sun and objects that seemed to bathe in it. The second time I saw the light was not in real life, but in one of my dreams, where it felt like my heart was stopping. I walked toward this light, which was behind a door. It was a very pleasant, bright, warm light that didn't blind. I knew that if I opened the door, the entire space would be flooded with that light, but as soon as I started to open it, I woke up.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm, I felt like I was with one foot in that world and the other in the spiritual world. My consciousness seemed to be in different places simultaneously.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: Many different ones. Specifically during my main experience, I mainly felt disappointment in my life, shame, and guilt. In other experiences that happened later, there were also many positive emotions and spiritual tremors.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt united or one with the world
elements.Did you suddenly seem to understand ever: Everything about myself or others, I described everything in detail in the story of my experiences.
elements.Did scenes from your past come back to y: I remembered many things I had long forgotten and never recalled, but that were real. The experience healed me and the wounds from the past.
elements.Did scenes from the future come to you?: Scenes from my personal future, There were many premonitions about future events or my relationships with loved ones. I didn't know exactly how or what would happen, but I understood everything when it did. Signs and warnings hinted at betrayals and destructive relationships. Later, it all happened, and I already knew what the signs were warning about. There were also blessed premonitions, which also came true.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Unaffiliated- Atheist, I used to be a believer. But, by the time these events started, I had already been an atheist for several years.
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, Now I even look forward to death in some sense, as a return home. Though now I will never again forcefully try to hasten this moment.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I felt the justification and necessity of what was happening. Even though it was difficult and heavy, it was exactly what pierced my consciousness. I needed a 'push' from outside, otherwise I would have changed nothing in my life, although I often wanted to.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I became more empathetic, started helping more (without sacrificing my health or compromising my values), became more understanding of others, and began valuing myself.
elements.Did you seem to encounter a mystical bei: I heard a voice I could not identify, I heard in the bus at times a repeating phrase "Jesus is nearby" and background meditative noise.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, There was a moment on the plane with a sense of unity, and there was another experience that showed me the interconnectedness of people. There were also experiences with prayers, when my prayers influenced other people.
elements.During your experience, did you gain spe: Uncertain, Absolutely every life is important, even if we don't understand now what influence we have on other people, it doesn't mean it's not there. Even a small random word said to another person can change the lives of thousands of people.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, I gained awareness of my life's purpose. To learn to love and help others. To learn to forgive others and even myself, even when it's unbearably hard. To carry this light, which God ignited in me and other people, because it's important. And to pray for myself and, if possible, for others. And what's very important, for the dead too.

Yes, Signs from the lanterns during the crossing showed me signs related to God after the sign of death. By this point, I can no longer recall everything specifically, but this part ended with drawings related to God. I'm not sure if this is a vague memory, but there seems to have been another drawing of a flower, something like a lotus, symbolizing paradise for me. It was like a promise of eternal life if I chose God during my life. That's why I was led to confession, albeit in such an unusual way.
Yes, Everything works together for good.
Yes, In any life situation, one must learn to act out of love.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: My drawings are coming to life, though not always literally. Sometimes it happens with my words that I wrote. Sometimes my dreams and intentions materialize, sometimes even instantly. I began to feel a constant connection with God, frequent communication with Him, and understanding His will regarding me. My dreams changed significantly, becoming connected to my spiritual growth. I didn't have such dreams before. I became a believer. No, not like that. I became knowing. I no longer just believe in God, I know that He exists and guides me. Relationships with people changed too - all unnecessary things faded away while necessary ones appeared. I began to feel the degree of people's sincerity and their intentions. Many old things became foreign to me. I started distancing myself from people who drag me down, use me, or distance me from God. Even if it's a friendship that lasted for years, even if it's family members I've known all my life. It became much easier. All acquaintances said something changed in me, something they don't understand and can't explain. Some friends even stopped looking me in the eye. My presence began to confuse them, an awkwardness appeared that wasn't there before. I started praying often, sometimes spontaneously by inner calling. God showed me the power of prayer. I began studying the experiences of people who went through something similar. This further completed the picture and allowed deeper understanding of what happened to me and what's happening. I changed jobs, started listening more to intuition and inner voice, understanding what's beneficial for me and what's not. I began standing up for my convictions, setting boundaries, and leaving if I'm not happy. Many convictions changed, as did life values.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, Almost all relationships with people were destroyed, but some on the contrary strengthened.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, No words can fully convey what I experienced. There are simply no suitable words.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, All my transcendent experiences completely eclipsed real life. I don't remember anything in such detail and vivid colors as everything that happened in those experiences, as if what I experienced was more real than my entire life.
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Yes, Drawings and words became prophetic, dreams became spiritual.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Uncertain, I'd heard about the light at the end of the tunnel. And that's about it.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, Supernatural events continue happening to me to this day, which further complement the knowledge, understanding and feelings that opened up to me. They don't contradict them but rather open my eyes to what I didn't fully understand or give me new knowledge based on previous ones.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, Same reason. God continues conversing with me.
elements.At any time in your life, has anything e: Uncertain, I still have moments of connection with God, sometimes spontaneously and sometimes intentionally sought.
